title: "Native Drake Torque Replay"

# Native Drake Torque Replay

## Calculation and Scope

The F06b primitive restores the complete numeric discrete state of an owned,
collision-free URDF plant and replays frozen post-limit revolute motor torques.
It consumes Tools' canonical `ExperimentReplayBundle` through the UD seam.
The native actuation matrix maps ordered motor inputs to generalized effort:
\(\tau=B u\). Each interval audits actual native net actuation before
stepping; the independent replay accepts no feedback or observations.

All admitted motors have one input, finite positive effort limits, and a
unit SimpleTransmission. Drake ignores nonunit URDF mechanical reductions;
the adapter rejects those declarations. Collision geometry, mimic joints,
extensions and external resources require other policies and fail admission.
Unactuated coordinates remain native dynamic states. This slice does not
qualify contact, muscle actuation, full-body anatomy or six-engine parity.

## State and Numerical Policy

Configuration and tangent velocity retain their distinct native dimensions.
The synthetic floating-base fixture has eight positions and seven velocities.
The complete discrete vector must contain finite values, and floating-base
quaternions must already have unit norm within absolute tolerance `1e-12`.
Invalid quaternions fail rather than being normalized.

The native plant uses fixed discrete steps, unsampled output ports, and the
actual recorded discrete contact solver and approximation. Unsampled ports
avoid the native abstract output-history state. Continuous state, abstract
state and unexpected discrete layouts are rejected. The adapter restores
state, initializes the native Simulator once, verifies initialization did
not alter it, and advances to every requested boundary without resetting.
Input row \(u_k\) is held on each interval; the final unused sentinel must
equal the preceding row. Torque limits must already have been applied.

Drake 1.57.0 also has abstract *parameters*. An owned factory-default context
admits its recorded boolean prefix and the two empty internal constraint
maps only. Public native constraint queries must prove zero constraints;
another version or layout requires review. Caller-supplied contexts and
parameter changes are unavailable through this API. Numeric parameter
identity hashes little-endian IEEE754 bytes, preserving native unused NaN
sentinels without inserting nonfinite JSON values or altering parameters.
Finite state and output remain mandatory.

## Identity and Evidence

Identity binds source URDF bytes, loaded topology and numeric/default-parameter
identity, ordered native actuator channels, timestep, solver/approximation,
adapter source and loaded parsing, plant, tree and analysis modules.
Shared native admission helper bytes are included in both engine provider
identities; Tools remains the sole replay-schema authority. A fresh
execution plant is independently checked again after bundle validation.
This is not complete transitive-library or source-to-binary attestation.

Eleven tests pass with actual Drake 1.57.0 and Python 3.12 on local Linux.
A saturated synthetic feedback rollout is reproduced by a fresh replay
within absolute configuration/velocity tolerance `1e-12`, with exact initial
state and independently queried motor effort. Negative checks cover missing
state, invalid quaternion, effort/grid violations, changed source, unsupported
model declarations and terminal input. This same-provider deterministic
agreement does not establish integration convergence or a mocap match.

## Primary Sources and Remaining Gates

The [native Simulator documentation](https://drake.mit.edu/doxygen_cxx/classdrake_1_1systems_1_1_simulator.html)
defines initialization and event boundaries. The
[URDF parsing policy](https://drake.mit.edu/doxygen_cxx/group__multibody__parsing.html)
describes transmission limitations; the
[v1.57.0 plant source](https://github.com/RobotLocomotion/drake/blob/v1.57.0/multibody/plant/multibody_plant.cc)
defines default constraint parameter maps. Source review supports this
restricted policy and does not prove binary equivalence.

F06 remains open for model variants, full-horizon provider integration,
step refinement, contact/grip and the all-engine denominator. F07/F08 retain
muscle feasibility and private-capture acceptance. Reproduction and failed
experiments are recorded in `F06_DRAKE_NATIVE_TURNOVER.md`.
